item.title: SCP-5645:
item.content:encoded:
There are a number of problems here, but the primary one is that this is merely a description.

SCPs are speculative fiction stories presented in the form of archival documents. Some are vignettes that paint an evocative scene over the course of a few paragraphs, some are sweeping multiple act novellas with twisting plots, some tell their stories through the ways that they toy with the framing itself… but at its core, every SCP is a story. That is the point of an SCP.

item.content:encoded: Hold up a sec; how calm this SCP be bad? I mean, there's nothing wrong with it at all; I mean, if it was because of its description, then why does it even matter? The point of SCP is that they were meant to be bizarre and have abilities that makes no sense in our world.

item.title: SCP-4576:
item.content:encoded:
I don't think there was any way it could have been expressed in the text in a way for me to completely get it without whacking normal readers over the head with the blunt end of the premise, so I think its fine as it is.

I really enjoyed it, and thanks for your explanation, since I usually read too hard into things about 99% of the time (I thought the scarecrow had been lost, and time-traveled to the future to get revenge, only to realize that time-traveling to the future caused it to be lost to Kid Lana when it looked back, causing it to go back again in the bright flash, but it doesn't arrive and clear up the misunderstanding, setting off the chain of events).

Thanks!

item.title: Live At Death: Re: Staff Post - Deletion Vote
SCP-3648:
item.content:encoded:
I have the same problem with this that I do with a lot of "[religious, folk lore, or pop cultural thing] is back, in SCP format" articles. Namely, that much of the enjoyment and understanding that is derived from the specific ways in which the story is told and uses its medium. Stripped of the specific story-telling context, and not adapted to the medium of a SCP document, it loses almost all of its value as anything but a reference. Just as I wouldn't be interested in reading The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, The SCP Article, I wasn't particularly interested in reading this.

I will say that I enjoyed the dreamy quality of the recovered footage, but the article overall did little to nothing for me.

item.title: SCP-1648:
item.content:encoded:
This article has several handfuls of concepts that seem to have been pulled out of a hat - technicolor bats! cute names! mechanical geniuses! hats! not understanding basic concepts! That's not inherently a bad thing, but there's no narrative or even strong image/concept that can tie all these elements together.

The effect is like finding a heap of random clothes at Goodwill and being told that it's an outfit. -1

item.title: SCP-648:
item.content:encoded:
I was attempting to judge this solely on the context in which it was written, meaning no reference to later executions that took "anomalous other-space" in more interesting directions. So it's pretty funny to open the comments and see the exact same complaints leveled at it at the time of writing.

I liked a few of the strange touches (eternal twilight, attack from inside, the unbelievably Series 1 phrase "anomalous slipperiness of the wall"), but it's just not enough to sustain the article. -1
